advisor.commerce.caveats: Freight routes and ports are not yet built for the Malaysia edition.
advisor.culture.caveats: Faith, wonders and disasters are not yet built for the Malaysia edition.
advisor.explorer.caveats: Population is DOSM's {year} mid-year estimate by administrative district. Six districts created in 2025 (Membakut in Sabah; Gedong, Lingga, Pantu, Sebuyau and Siburan in Sarawak) are counted in the districts they were carved from, so every figure sits on the 160 districts the map draws.
Cities are, for now, districts of 150,000 or more residents, named after their largest town; conurbations that span several districts (Greater Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Johor Bahru) are not yet joined.
almanac.resources_intro: Resource markers show power plants of 25 MW or more as the World Resources Institute listed them in 2019, named oil, gas and LNG sites that Wikidata places in Malaysia, and the districts where durian, coconut, pineapple or sago cover at least 800–1,500 ha (DOSM, 2024). Oil and gas fields at sea are shown on the nearest coast hex. Not on the map: mines (open data gives output by state, not positions), and oil palm, rubber and paddy (published by state, not by district). Press R to show or hide them.
advisor.energy.caveats: Power plants are those of 25 MW or more in WRI's Global Power Plant Database v1.3.0 (2019): plants built or closed since are not reflected, and Sarawak's large hydro stations (Bakun, Murum) are missing from it.
Some stations may be listed twice in the database (Tanjung Bin appears as two coal rows at one site; Kapar's coal and its gas row are the same company), so a state's mapped capacity can overstate it.
Oil, gas and LNG sites are the few Wikidata lists with coordinates: most Petronas fields are not on the map, and no output figures are available.
Mines are not mapped: the Department of Mineral and Geoscience publishes output by state, with no positions.
advisor.land.caveats: Land cover is the Sentinel-2 10 m map sampled at 7 points per hex, so small features blur into their surroundings.

That map classes oil palm and rubber plantations as trees, so forest is overstated and crops understated, most in Johor, Pahang, Perak, Sabah and Sarawak. Oil palm (MPOB) and rubber area are published by state, not by district, and rubber not at all in open data.
Forest reserve area is the state's gazetted permanent reserved forest (Forestry Department): it is not a land-cover share.
